text: Hello to all of our viewers. Ladies and
gentlemen, we are witnessing the
tightening of the U.S. noose around
Iran, revealing the vulnerabilities of
the Islamic Republic regime. In recent
days, numerous Iranian police officials
and security personnel have filmed
videos complaining that they haven't
received their salaries and are living
in such dire poverty that they cannot
afford milk or food for their families,
pleading for their wages to be paid.
Meanwhile, higher-ranking officials
continue to preach to their
subordinates to keep fighting and to
continue to die as martyrs. They claim
that after martyrdom, they will go to
meet 72 virgins. However, what is the
truth? Distinguished American historian
Professor Victor David Hanson has
pointed out that many high-ranking
Iranian officials have taken billions
of dollars to go and enjoy themselves
in Paris and London. Professor Victor
David Hanson says that while the people
are starving, the Iranian elite are
living like kings. Iran preaches that
it holds a moral, intellectual, and
religious superiority over anyone else
in both the Islamic and Western worlds.
They also claim to be the purest
followers of Islam. They follow Sharia
law. They do not drink alcohol, they do
not smoke, and they do not collect
interest. But they are also the most
corrupt regime. Therefore, all those
among the theocratic elite in Iran own
homes in the United Kingdom, in London,
and in Paris. They hold billions of
dollars in foreign bank accounts. Their
children all attend preparatory schools
. Their children are professors,
doctors, and professionals of that
nature in the United States. And as
such, they are also the most corrupt of
all Islamic regimes. And they talk
about wanting to die at any moment and
ascend to heaven to be with 72 virgins.
But the elite do not want to do that.
They do not want to kill, nor do they
want to commit suicide. Because they
are siphoning off the entirety of
Iran's oil revenue and living like
kings abroad. The Iranian government
follows a mystical, apocalyptic version
of Shia Islam. In the Middle East
region, they are inherently a minority
and they are not Arabs, they are
Persians. That is why there have been
natural rifts among the 93 million
people within Iran. People with a
glorious history of dominating the Arab
world and they have a religion
different from the majority of the
region. Although we all know that only
60%of Iranians are Persian, there are
also others such as Kurds, Assyrians,
and all sorts of other people in it.
The Iranian clerical regime believes
they are the purest followers of Islam.
Because they believe they are the
purest followers of Islam and have a
superior Islamic faith compared to
their neighbors. And because, as
Persian chauvinists superior to Arabs,
they deserve to inherit the crown—not
the Arabs, the guardians of Mecca, but
rather they should be the spokespeople
for the entire Middle East. Therefore,
since the 1980 Islamic Revolution, they
have tried to create what they call the
Islamic crescent, a Shia crescent. And
that means we will have Iran and then
we will take Syria, a branch closer to
Shia than Sunni. And then we will
control all of Iraq. And then we will
take all of Syria as well. Next, we
will have Hezbollah to infiltrate and
in fact take control of Lebanon, which
is what they have been doing. And then
we will have the Houthis, an unorthodox
branch in Yemen. And then we will take
the West Bank and the Gaza Strip
through Hamas. Who are Sunni Arabs but
support Iran. Ultimately, Iran wants to
transform into the only Islamic power
that can destroy Jewish Israel and gain
control of the Middle East. And thanks
to that resurgence, all the minorities
in Iraq, in Kuwait, in the UAE, and
across the Gulf will flock under Iran's
banner, and that is Iran's calculation
right now. That is why, while the
people are starving, the clerics in
Iran are still calling for war with the
US. A senior advisor to the
commander-in-chief of Iran's Islamic
Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) stated
that Tehran has so far only conducted
conventional warfare and has not yet
engaged in asymmetric warfare. Which he
suggested could mean war on Wall Street
in Manhattan and anywhere, at any time
on U.S. soil. This person's name is
Mohammad Reza Naqdi. He claimed that
over 90%of the Islamic Republic of
Iran's missile arsenal remains intact
and warned that any new U.S. attack
would come at a very high price. Naqdi
also said, "We are fulfilling the
commitments announced by the Supreme
National Security Council, but the
enemy must know that if they attack us,
they will pay a very heavy price." The
Islamic Republic of Iran's missile
production network is highly resilient
and self-sufficient. He claimed that
the relationship between the
Revolutionary Guard and the government
is also in its best state and is very
strong. Indeed, we are seeing the
government branch represented by
President Masoud Pezeshkian attending
the Shanghai Cooperation Organization
summit, where he is there to meet
Russian President Putin and Chinese
President Xi Jinping. Therefore,
Professor Victor Davis Hanson has
pointed out that this is an axis of
aggression that wants to dominate the
world, including Russia, China, and
Iran. Professor Victor Davis Hanson's
verbatim words were that Putin said the
greatest tragedy of the 20th century
was the collapse of the Soviet Union.
He said that as a fascist dictator, an
authoritarian totalitarian dictator.
But what he meant by that statement is
that we Russians ran almost the entire
world except for the United States, and
we want to return to that era. And
after the collapse of the Soviet Union,
the West deceived us. He believes so,
believes in allowing all these
republics to become independent, and
our population dropped from 250 million
to 140 million, and we were weakened.
So, my job as Vladimir Putin, he thinks
, is to restore the glory of Russia
under the Tsars, defined by having the
same territory and power as Russia
under the Soviet Union, led by
dictators just like himself. Putin
thought that we have all this oil that
the West doesn't have, and we control
Venezuela, and we are present all over
the world to oppose the United States.
We are also collaborating with China.
Then he asked himself how he could
weaken the United States and reclaim
glory for Russia. So in 2008, he moved
into Georgia and stopped that
separation. If we notice, we will see
that in everything he has done, he
always advances when a president is
weak. President George Bush was tied
down in Afghanistan and Iraq. And then
Putin moved in under Barack Obama to
seize the Crimean Peninsula. However,
in 2016-17, as we know, Donald Trump
appeared and said, "I have a bigger
button than you, bigger than Kim Jong
Un and Putin." This sounded crazy. But
in fact, Putin did not do anything
crazy for four years. And then Putin
saw Biden, he sensed an opening, and
moved in to take Kyiv. So it can be
said that Putin is an opportunist, and
he thinks that whenever he sees a weak
Europe, he strikes. Take the Nord
Stream pipeline and make them dependent
on our natural gas. Professor Victor
Davis Hanson also answered the question
: is there anyone in Russia today who
could stage a coup and overthrow
Vladimir Putin? We have often asked
ourselves if a coup could actually
happen in Russia. I do not believe
there will be a coup against Putin
because the only person who could
overthrow him is someone even more
far-right than he is. It’s like
Prigozhin, the former leader of the
Wagner Group. When it seemed like he
was about to organize a coup, it was a
right-wing coup. He said, "You are not
being tough enough in conducting this
war.""You are a bunch of cowards." He
pointed directly at Shoigu and
Gerasimov to say that. But that is the
far-right group, also the group that
Putin fears most. The ultra-nationalist
extremists. While Putin has imprisoned
those we call more moderate, people
like Navalny, Alexei Navalny, who was
murdered in prison, and others. So he
has wiped out the pro-Western, moderate
opposition. So now in Russia, one could
say there is no one left. And the only
critics are on the hard right, the
hardline nationalists who are saying he
is too weak, meaning they are even more
hawkish than Putin. So what about the
Russian people? Many Russian citizens
now openly call Putin Hitler. And we
have just had a report from The
Economist saying that Putin fears that
if he fails in Ukraine, he will be
hanged. Indeed, right now Putin is very
afraid for his life. The dictator is
strengthening his security detail for
the fourth time since the war began.
The bunker king has increased the
number of staff at the FSO headquarters
from 785 to 812 people. Before the
full-scale war broke out, the staff of
this agency had not changed for nearly
13 years. However, since the war broke
out, it has changed four times.
According to the Financial Times, the
Russian dictator has cut down on his
trips. At the same time, security
checks for those meeting him have
become much stricter. Additionally,
sources from the Financial Times also
stated that Putin and his family appear
less frequently at their residences in
Moscow and Valdai. Instead, they prefer
to stay at secure facilities. Below is
what a famous Russian doctor shared
about Putin and the reason why this
doctor calls Putin Hitler. This is the
famous doctor Natalia Polyakova, and
she said, "I openly compared Putin to
Hitler because at 7:00 a.m. on June 4,
2026, FSB agents arrived at my house
with a court order." They searched my
house for an hour, then took my laptop
and both of my phones. I am a doctor
specializing in clinical diagnostic
testing. After my maternity leave, I
was invited to head the lab at
Correctional Facility No. 32, a prison
for female tuberculosis patients. They
told me the work there would be quiet
and no one would bother me. The
equipment there was as outdated as it
was in the 1990s. I had to learn how to
manually count every white and red
blood cell by eye under a microscope.
Each technician had to test about 20
patients every day. In the shared staff
kitchen, they played Solovyov’s show
on the radio. In it, he called for
people to have 48 hours to leave Kyiv,
then to flatten the city, neighborhood
by neighborhood. I said plainly that it
was fascist propaganda and compared
Putin to Hitler. They listened to me
and smiled. The next day, my boss
called me in and said someone had come
to see him. He warned me that our
conversations were forbidden. They said
I had signed papers listing topics that
weren't allowed to be discussed, but I
never had. Only then did they make me
sign and read that list. But after that
, my colleagues started avoiding me.
Some no longer ate lunch with me.
Others stopped talking to me entirely.
We knew very well which prisoners were
informants watching us to report back
to security. I refused to voluntarily
donate part of my salary to the war
fund. A month later, my boss said
Moscow had called and ordered him to
fire me, calling me an unreliable
element. The officers showed me
screenshots of my Telegram account,
including a photo of Navalny. Two
officers pressured me relentlessly for
hours. They asked if I had relatives in
Ukraine and why I refused to donate
money for the war. I said I had a sick
child and had other priorities. They
threatened to hand my file over to the
FSB for discrediting the army. I had to
rewrite my resignation letter five
times. A year later, when FSB agents
searched my home again, one of them
looked at my daughter and said, "She's
so cute, what's your name?" Then he
asked me if I understood why they were
there. They held me at the FSB
headquarters for six hours. An
investigator questioned me for about
five or ten minutes. They typed my
answers into the computer and left the
room for about 20 minutes before
returning to continue. Two weeks later,
I went to retrieve my devices. I had to
wait outside the FSB headquarters for
40 minutes. He said that my laptop and
phone had been sent to Cross NO for
inspection. He also warned me not to
come here again. Either we will come to
see you, or we will call you. Every
morning I woke up, I would anxiously
wait to see if they would show up at my
door at 7 a.m. I received my passport
just in time and left with my daughter
the next day. I don't want to pass this
fear on to my children, but I will have
to carry it for the rest of my life. We
move on to some developments on the
battlefield, as today we have entered
September. Thus, Russia's entire spring
and summer offensive phase has failed,
with Russian losses reaching over
200,000 soldiers. This is the latest
report from United 24 Media, citing
sources from the Ministry of Defense of
Ukraine. They stated that Russia
entered the spring of 2026 with the
expectation of creating a major
breakthrough on the battlefield. But
six months later, that breakthrough has
yet to appear. Moscow has lost over
200,000 troops, including those killed
and wounded. During the spring and
summer, they did not successfully
execute any mechanized assaults and
only gained very little territory.
Meanwhile, the Ukrainian military
liberated 745 km² in the south in May
2026, which was supposed to be the
start of a major offensive expected to
yield results at least equal to the
2024-2025 period. The Russian military
gained more territory in previous years
and intended to build on that momentum,
specifically aiming to capture the
entire Donetsk region and gain leverage
to pressure Kyiv. However, in just the
first three days of launching combat
operations, the Russian military
suffered over 5,000 casualties. By
mid-March, the situation made it clear
that there would be no significant
progress. According to the General
Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine,
by the end of March, Russia had lost
approximately 1.3 million troops since
the start of the invasion, and by the
end of last month. This figure had
risen to 1.84 million killed and
wounded. The Russian military is losing
soldiers at a record pace. Over 100,000
people in the spring and another
100,000 in the summer of 2026 became
casualties. Notably, July 2026 was the
month the Russian military suffered its
heaviest manpower losses of the year,
with 42,860 casualties. This was also
the highest monthly loss for the
Russian military since January 2025. In
total, Russia lost 238,650 troops in
the first seven months of 2026. At the
same time, equipment losses also
reached record levels, with nearly
14,000 units in just one month. Yet,
Russia still failed to execute a single
successful mechanized assault, meaning
an attack using tanks and armored
vehicles. The Ukrainian military
repelled every such attack by using
drones and organizing effective
defenses across various sections of the
front. But the clearest evidence of the
campaign's failure is not just the
scale of Russia's losses, but the
meager territory the Kremlin gained
after those losses. Mr. Pavlo Palisa,
Deputy Head of the Office of the
President of Ukraine, stated that the
Russian military is advancing very
slowly and barely gaining any
additional territory. We are seeing a
trend where the enemy's pace of
advancement is slowing down. In some
months, the area captured by Russian
forces may only be a few dozen square
kilometers, according to data from
public sources, including Ukraine's
public open-source intelligence
analysis project, DeepState. Conversely
, the Ukrainian military has achieved
very concrete results. By the end of
2025, they had liberated areas
surrounding Kupyansk in Kharkiv Oblast.
And in the first half of 2026, the
Ukrainian military conducted offensive
operations in the south, liberating 745
km² of territory and 26 settlements in
the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, and
Zaporizhzhia regions. A major reason
for the failure of Russia's offensive
campaign is the shift in the
battlefield balance due to the dense
presence of drones in the sky.
Ukraine's defense system is now capable
of intercepting infantry assaults as
they approach, before they can gather
into large-scale attacks. Attacks by
armored columns, which just a few years
ago were a primary method for breaking
through front lines, are now rarely
carried out because they are too
vulnerable to drone strikes. Another
factor is operations using medium-range
attack drones. These operations
continuously disrupt Russian supply
systems in the rear, 50 to 200 km from
the front line. In May 2026 alone,
these types of drones struck
approximately 350 targets. In May 2026,
similar strikes hit Russian supply
systems in Luhansk Oblast and supply
lines heading toward the Crimean
Peninsula. Fully under Ukrainian fire
control, fuel tankers, trucks, and
other vehicles are frequently struck
along supply routes. And by summer,
medium-range attack operations
effectively allowed Ukraine to
completely isolate the Crimean
Peninsula. As a result, the Russians
have been unable to ensure sufficient
ammunition, fuel, and equipment are
delivered on time to their offensive
forces. Supply systems are disrupted
while a significant force must be
diverted to air defense and restoring
supply lines, leaving Russian resources
further stretched. Given the current
battlefield situation, the Ukrainian
military believes Russia will be unable
to break the fortress belt in Donetsk
Oblast, a task Putin has assigned the
Russian army to complete by late 2026
or early 2027. The evidence is that for
many months, the Chasiv Yar area in
Donetsk Oblast has remained one of the
most difficult sectors on the front.
The areas surrounding Doblopilia and
Druzhkivka are also under increasing
pressure from Russia. But despite
months of attacks, Kostiantynivka
remains under Ukrainian control. This
Kostiantynivka area is one of four
major cities in Donetsk province that
form a defensive fortress belt,
including Kostiantynivka, Druzhkivka,
Sloviansk, and Kramatorsk. Russia wants
to capture these cities to pave the way
for an advance into the rest of the
province still held by Ukraine. Deputy
Head of President Zelenskyy's Office,
Mr. Palisa, stated that Russia's
political leadership expects to capture
the entire Donetsk province by or on
December 31, 2026. While the military
requested a bit more time until the end
of May 2027, that is unrealistic. Mr.
Palisa said the area has been under
constant pressure for months, but the
Ukrainian military continues to halt
the Russian advance. Ladies and
gentlemen, despite facing pressure both
domestically and internationally, we
have heard Indian Prime Minister
Narendra Modi call on Putin to end the
war. The Russian people have started
calling Putin a fascist, and they have
begun to resist. They have started to
protest against spending money on
donations for the military. So, will
Mr. Putin stop the war? Or will he
continue to pursue the goal of
capturing the entire Donetsk province
and the entire Donbas region before
stopping? I invite you to help Danny by
leaving your thoughts in the comments
section below. Danny would like to
thank you and see you again in the next
program. Thank you very much.
